notes:
I couldn't write these notes because I wasn't able to read any of the sources.

My first attempt to run ten searches at once went over the tool's usage limit. When I retried with one search, the tool told me I had no calls left for this turn. So I didn't open a single page on enduringword.com, biblehub.com, studylight.org, preceptaustin.org or any of the other approved sites.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and to give a URL for every point. Writing from memory would break those rules, so I haven't drafted anything for any verse. That includes the parts people often write about, like the seventy years (v. 10) and how "plans to prosper you" (v. 11) gets used.

When you ask again, I'll search a few sites at a time so I stay under the limit, roughly in this order:
1. **Verse by verse:** Enduring Word on Jeremiah 29; Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub or StudyLight; Precept Austin.
2. **Verses that get the most attention:**
   - v. 7: The Gospel Coalition, Desiring God, Ligonier.
   - vv. 11–13: Got Questions, Desiring God, Grace to You (gty.org), Seedbed.
   - vv. 10 and 14: Spurgeon's sermons.
3. **Other views:** NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey; Catholic and Orthodox sources; whatever these sites say about prosperity-style readings of v. 11.

I'll leave out any verse where I can't find a source.
